title: "Tries and Prefix Trees"

# Tries and Prefix Trees

A **Trie** (derived from "re**trie**val"), also known as a **prefix tree**, is a specialized tree structure where each edge represents a character of a string key. All descendants of a node share a common string prefix. In Go, the boring default for string lookup is `map[string]T`, but a Trie shines when you need to match prefixes, validate autocomplete options, or perform IP routing lookups in $O(L)$ time where $L$ is the string length, completely independent of how many millions of keys exist.

## Mental model

Unlike a binary tree where nodes store whole strings, Trie nodes store transition characters. Shared prefixes share identical parent paths:

```
                  (Root)
                 /      \
               "c"      "t"
               /          \
             "a"          "e"
            /   \           \
          "r"   "t"         "a"
           |     |           |
        (cart) (cat)       (tea)
```

- Keys: `"cart"`, `"cat"`, `"tea"`
- Searching for `"car"`: Follow root $\to$ `'c'` $\to$ `'a'` $\to$ `'r'`. It exists as a prefix, but whether it is a complete word depends on the boolean flag `isTerminal`.
- Autocomplete: Walk down to the node matching the prefix (e.g. `'c'` $\to$ `'a'`), then gather all terminal descendants (`"cart"`, `"cat"`).

Search and insertion cost $O(L)$ operations where $L$ is the length of the word, which is ideal for desk SKU catalogs with hundreds of thousands of items.

## Worked examples

### Case 1: Desk SKU and Tag Autocomplete Trie

Save as `trie_desk.go`. Implement a generic Trie capable of storing desk SKU metadata and providing prefix autocompletion.

```go
// trie_desk.go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
)

type TrieNode[T any] struct {
	children   map[rune]*TrieNode[T]
	isTerminal bool
	value      T
}

func newTrieNode[T any]() *TrieNode[T] {
	return &TrieNode[T]{
		children: make(map[rune]*TrieNode[T]),
	}
}

type Trie[T any] struct {
	root *TrieNode[T]
	size int
}

func NewTrie[T any]() *Trie[T] {
	return &Trie[T]{root: newTrieNode[T]()}
}

func (t *Trie[T]) Insert(key string, val T) {
	curr := t.root
	for _, ch := range key {
		if _, exists := curr.children[ch]; !exists {
			curr.children[ch] = newTrieNode[T]()
		}
		curr = curr.children[ch]
	}
	if !curr.isTerminal {
		t.size++
	}
	curr.isTerminal = true
	curr.value = val
}

func (t *Trie[T]) Search(key string) (T, bool) {
	curr := t.root
	for _, ch := range key {
		next, exists := curr.children[ch]
		if !exists {
			var zero T
			return zero, false
		}
		curr = next
	}
	if curr.isTerminal {
		return curr.value, true
	}
	var zero T
	return zero, false
}

func (t *Trie[T]) StartsWith(prefix string) bool {
	curr := t.root
	for _, ch := range prefix {
		next, exists := curr.children[ch]
		if !exists {
			return false
		}
		curr = next
	}
	return true
}

func (t *Trie[T]) AutoComplete(prefix string) []string {
	curr := t.root
	for _, ch := range prefix {
		next, exists := curr.children[ch]
		if !exists {
			return nil
		}
		curr = next
	}

	var results []string
	collectWords(curr, prefix, &results)
	return results
}

func collectWords[T any](node *TrieNode[T], current string, results *[]string) {
	if node.isTerminal {
		*results = append(*results, current)
	}
	for ch, child := range node.children {
		collectWords(child, current+string(ch), results)
	}
}

func main() {
	catalog := NewTrie[string]()

	catalog.Insert("DESK-CHAIR", "Ergonomic Mesh Chair")
	catalog.Insert("DESK-LAMP", "LED Adjustable Lamp")
	catalog.Insert("DESK-MAT", "Leather Desk Pad")
	catalog.Insert("DESK-DRAWER", "Under-desk organizer")
	catalog.Insert("DISH-TOWEL", "Barista cleanup towel")

	// Exact search
	sku := "DESK-LAMP"
	if desc, found := catalog.Search(sku); found {
		fmt.Printf("Exact SKU lookup [%s]: %s\n", sku, desc)
	}

	// Prefix check
	pfx := "DESK-"
	fmt.Printf("Any items starting with '%s'? %t\n", pfx, catalog.StartsWith(pfx))

	// Autocomplete recommendations
	suggestions := catalog.AutoComplete("DESK-")
	fmt.Println("\nAutocomplete options for 'DESK-':")
	for _, s := range suggestions {
		desc, _ := catalog.Search(s)
		fmt.Printf("  • %s (%s)\n", s, desc)
	}
}
```

Run:

```bash
go run trie_desk.go
```

Output:

```
Exact SKU lookup [DESK-LAMP]: LED Adjustable Lamp
Any items starting with 'DESK-'? true

Autocomplete options for 'DESK-':
  • DESK-CHAIR (Ergonomic Mesh Chair)
  • DESK-LAMP (LED Adjustable Lamp)
  • DESK-MAT (Leather Desk Pad)
  • DESK-DRAWER (Under-desk organizer)
```

## The trap

A common temptation in textbook Trie implementations is using a fixed ASCII array `[26]*TrieNode` for child pointers. While this avoids map allocations, it panics on uppercase letters, digits, dashes, and UTF-8 characters (`ch - 'a' < 0`). In Go, strings are UTF-8 by default; using `map[rune]*TrieNode` safely handles spaces, punctuation, dashes, and non-English characters without buffer overruns.

```go
// bad_ascii_trie.go
package main

import "fmt"

type BadNode struct {
	children [26]*BadNode // TRAP: Only supports lowercase a-z
}

func badInsert(root *BadNode, word string) {
	curr := root
	for _, ch := range word {
		// If word contains '-' or '0'..'9', index goes out of range!
		idx := ch - 'a'
		if idx < 0 || idx >= 26 {
			fmt.Printf("PANIC PREVENTED: rune '%c' is invalid for [26] array!\n", ch)
			return
		}
		if curr.children[idx] == nil {
			curr.children[idx] = &BadNode{}
		}
		curr = curr.children[idx]
	}
}

func main() {
	root := &BadNode{}
	badInsert(root, "DESK-101")
}
```

Run:

```bash
go run bad_ascii_trie.go
```

Output:

```
PANIC PREVENTED: rune 'D' is invalid for [26] array!
```

## The boring rule

1. If you only look up exact keys, use Go's built-in `map[string]V`. A hash map is faster and uses less memory than a Trie for exact matches.
2. Use a Trie when the requirements demand **prefix queries**: `StartsWith`, auto-complete, longest-prefix routing, or spell checking.
3. Use `map[rune]*TrieNode` in Go to safely handle Unicode runes and symbols.
4. If memory is tight and paths have long unbranching chains, consider a Radix Tree (compact Trie) where common non-branching edges are merged into single strings.
